key_insight: In HVTN 704/HPTN 085, bacterial STI burden was high, and reported oral PrEP use was associated with higher STI incidence.
clinical_relevance: The findings support integrating multisite STI testing, treatment, counseling, and targeted prevention into HIV prevention services.
method: Post-hoc analysis of 2,687 men and transgender persons who have sex with men across four countries.
STI testing every six months, with optional access to oral PrEP.
Cox models examined associations between time-varying PrEP use and incident bacterial STIs.
evidence_signal: At enrollment, 27.9% had a bacterial STI; among those negative at baseline, incidence was 29.4 per 100 person-years, with higher incidence during PrEP use than non-use (HR 1.75; 95% CI 1.44–2.13).
watch_item: PrEP use was not randomized, so this association does not establish that PrEP caused higher STI incidence; this paper concerns HIV/STI prevention, not AI cancer drug discovery.
paper_title: Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections and Oral HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis Use in HVTN 704/HPTN 085
